title: A chat that hides nothing
eyebrow: The answer you never got, the command output you could not read, and the mode that came back as an error — all three are on your own screen now.

blocks.text: That exercise found a real weakness: the mode check was driving the tool with its own copy of the settings, so it would have stayed green while your own chat was refused. It drives the app now.

decisions.title: The chat has no list of messages it is willing to hear
decisions.why: A list is what lost your /compact answer, and would have lost the next one just as quietly. Anything the tool sends that this app has no name for is drawn as a line rather than dropped.

decisions.title: Everything is kept; only the loudness differs
decisions.why: A line hidden today must still be there when you press Ctrl+O. What that costs was measured rather than assumed, and each line is now cut to the same length a command's output is.

decisions.title: Ctrl+O, remembered for the browser and not for one chat
decisions.why: It is the key that does this in your terminal, and it is a way of reading rather than a property of one conversation.

decisions.title: A chat can switch into bypass, but never starts there
decisions.why: Two separate settings: one permits the switch, the other takes it. A chat still asks about everything until you pick otherwise, which was proved rather than reasoned about.

decisions.title: Chats already on your board are read again to gain their commands
decisions.why: Otherwise the fix would have reached only chats you have never opened, and the one you photographed would have stayed as it was. Only ever a chat this app has never run itself — one with real turns in it is the only copy of those.

next.if_nothing: It waits on your look; nothing else moves on it.
